subject: history
title: Black Power to Black Lives Matter
welcome_lead: After 1965: from Watts and the Black Panthers to twenty-first-century activism.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Black Power, urban unrest and the continuation of civil rights struggles.
final_note: You have followed the long arc to the present.

concepts.def: Slogan popularised by Stokely Carmichael in June 1966 emphasising racial pride and self-determination.
Founded by Bobby Seale and Huey Newton in October 1966 in Oakland, combining armed defence with social programmes.
1968 report on urban unrest concluding the US was 'moving toward two societies, one black, one white, separate and unequal'.
Killing of Martin Luther King Jr. on 4 April 1968 in Memphis, triggering nationwide unrest.
Policies, particularly from the 1965 Executive Order 11246, requiring federal contractors to hire without discrimination.
Movement founded in 2013 after George Zimmerman's acquittal in the killing of Trayvon Martin.

walkthroughs.body_html: Watts in August 1965, Newark and Detroit in 1967 exposed structural inequality. SNCC and CORE moved from integrationism to Black Power under Carmichael and Floyd McKissick. The Black Panther Party's ten-point programme demanded housing, education and ending police brutality. FBI COINTELPRO crippled the Panthers, killing Fred Hampton in December 1969. Internal splits and prosecutions weakened them by the mid-1970s.

Despite legal victories, persistent housing discrimination, police violence and labour market exclusion limited real gains. The 1968 Kerner Commission cited white racism, ghettoisation and unemployment. King's Poor People's Campaign signalled a shift to economic justice; his assassination on 4 April 1968 triggered riots in over 100 cities. The 1968 Fair Housing Act passed in the aftermath.

Historians including Jacquelyn Dowd Hall argue for a 'long civil rights movement' linking 1930s labour activism to twenty-first-century campaigns. The election of Barack Obama in 2008 was symbolic but did not end disparities. Black Lives Matter, founded after the 2013 acquittal in Trayvon Martin's killing, mobilised mass protests after Michael Brown (2014) and George Floyd (2020), reframing debates on policing and race.
